name: The Ancestor's Knucklebone
object: A knucklebone worn smooth by a hundred years of handling, threaded on gut string. Taken from the body of a Berserker who died fighting in the Borderlands and was never retrieved. It arrived in a collector's satchel through one of the Market Square arches, and nobody knows which world it came from, or who carried it through.
unlock: Defeat an enemy in single combat without any ally's assistance: no ally attacks it, heals you, or gives either of you a condition or advantage.
Keep one of the body's hand bones.
Spend a night alone with it before you sleep, and see how the ancestor fought.
risk: At dawn, make a WIL save, DC 12. On a failure, the ancestor's last fight plays out in you: take 1 Wound you do not remember taking, and whatever hunted them learns where you sleep.

resource.name: Fury Echo
resource.text: Fury Echo (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Fury Echo each time you tell a listener who has not heard it how the ancestor fought and fell, in full, over at least ten minutes. Echo never clears at a rest or when combat ends. Spent Echo returns only by telling it again to a new listener.

powers: Echo Strike (Free, while Raging, spend 1 Fury Echo): Roll a Fury Die and set it aside with the rest, up to your maximum. This does not use your Rage action. The die follows the Fury Die rules and is lost when your Rage ends.

Death's Door (Free, 1/encounter, when you Rage, spend all 3 Fury Echo): For this encounter, your Rage does not end when you drop to 0 HP. Your Fury Dice stay. You are still Dying, with all its rules, and Enduring Rage still applies once you have it. This is the bone's last act (see Escalation).
escalation: If you drop to 0 HP with Death's Door active, the knucklebone cracks at once and stops working. Your Rage still holds for the encounter. Replace it with another ancestor's relic from the Borderlands, or take one from a worthy enemy. The GM decides where it is and how long the search takes. Whatever hunted the ancestor learns the bone has moved. Roll a d6 on the table below, or choose.
design_note: Echo comes from a story told at a table, so the pool fills outside the fight and never from the Fury Dice the class already rolls. Death's Door is paid at the start of Rage, before the dangerous moment, and gives a first-echelon version of the level 18 Deep Rage.
notes: Reworked. Echo now fills by retelling, not by Fury Die matches (double-dipping); Death's Door paid up front (peak-value lethality); risk added; em dash removed; retelling venue: Sevenge and Gam's Public House (3_gazetteer). Unlock pass: risk now has a save and a Wound. Blind audit: 'assistance' defined; the escalation says the bone cracks at once while Rage holds. Audit round 6: Death's Door says you are still Dying.

name: The Loaded Die
object: An ivory gambling die with a tiny lead insert that makes it land on 6 roughly two-thirds of the time. Confiscated from a Black Hand card sharp at the Lower Reaches gambling house, then stolen from the evidence shelf at the Golden Knights' outpost. No paperwork exists for it. The card sharp has not stopped looking.
unlock: Win a wager against someone who genuinely believed they had the advantage: not a mark, not a fool, but someone who should have won.
Stake something you cannot afford to lose.
risk: After the wager, the loser makes an Insight check against your Influence check. If they win, they know the die was loaded, and they name you to the Black Hand card sharp.

resource.name: Fixes
resource.text: Fixes (pip tracker, max 4). Fixes do not refill automatically. To refill: run a game of chance during a Safe Rest and earn at least 1 silver in genuine winnings against an opponent who had a real chance of winning. Gain all 4 Fixes back. Safe Rests where you do not gamble leave the tracker as it is. Fixes return only this way.

powers: Fix (Free, before you roll an attack, spend 1 Fix): Declare you are using the die. Roll your Primary Die twice and take whichever result you prefer. This replaces your Primary Die only; advantage, disadvantage and extra dice from rushing are rolled normally. No memory required, both rolls happen now, in front of everyone.
Loaded Odds (Passive): Once per session, you may ask the GM whether a creature you can see is bluffing. The die rolls and the GM answers truthfully, but only yes or no.
escalation: When all 4 Fixes are spent, the die gets you anyway. On your next Vicious Opportunist use after depletion, the GM secretly rolls a d6. On a 1-3 the die turns on you: Vicious Opportunist does nothing, and that use is spent, and you do not know until after you have committed. The uncertainty lasts for one use only. Word that a loaded die is back in play reaches the card sharp within a session.
design_note: Mirrors Vicious Opportunist's loop of manipulating die results, but at a resource cost. Roll twice, pick best, needs no memory. Loaded Odds is social utility that costs nothing in stats. The escalation adds uncertainty for a class that is normally certain about when it cheats, and a pursuer.
notes: Risk line and a costly unlock step added; em dashes removed; escalation now brings the card sharp back. Left: Loaded Odds overlaps the Insight skill (detect lies); kept as free social utility per the spec. Audit: clearing rule stated ('Fixes return only this way'). name: The Battle Standard of the Nameless King
object: A black iron battle standard, the insignia ground off but the pole still bearing ghost-traces of a name no one can read. Found stacked with other confiscated relics in the Museum of Worlds Beyond storage vault. The curator will not release it without a writ. Three scholars have separately attempted to identify the insignia's origin and stopped work without explanation.
unlock: Lead a group of at least five non-party combatants to victory: soldiers, militia, hired swords, anyone you commanded in the field. The victory must be real, a fight that could have been lost.
Plant the standard yourself, in plain sight of the enemy.
risk: The first time you plant it, roll a d6. On a 1-3, someone in the watching crowd or the enemy ranks recognizes the standard, and the Knights of the Nameless King send an agent within two sessions.

resource.name: Authority
resource.text: Authority (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Authority whenever an ally within 4 spaces of the planted standard deals damage in a single attack equal to or greater than your level, at most 1 Authority per attack. Authority is strictly encounter-bound: all unspent pips are lost when combat ends, regardless of how many are held. It cannot be saved or stockpiled between encounters.

powers: Plant it (1 Action): Drive the standard into the ground within Reach 1. While it stands, allies within 4 spaces who can see it have advantage on their first attack each round. Spend 1 Authority to extend the aura by 2 spaces until your next turn.
Pull it (Free): The standard returns to your hand and the aura ends immediately.
Hold Ground (Reaction, spend 2 Authority): When the standard would be knocked over, stolen, or destroyed, it refuses. It cannot be moved by any force until the start of your next turn.
escalation: When you plant the standard a second time in one encounter, after it was pulled or knocked over, while Authority is at 0, the insignia becomes briefly legible to everyone present. The GM reads what it says aloud. It goes dark again immediately. What it says is the GM's tool: a name, a title, a command. Roll a d6 on the table below, or choose.
design_note: Authority triggers on a damage threshold, not on defeats, so no ally gains by stealing last hits. Any solid hit fills the pool, which rewards coordinated pressure. The escalation is pure City of Arches: the Nameless King's name appears once, and only the GM knows what it says.
notes: Risk line and a costly unlock step added; aura range stated in the resource line; em dashes removed. Left: Authority fills from allies' damage and clears at encounter end, so it has no world refill. This is the spec's own example of a good Commander item. Unlock pass: risk now a d6. Blind audit: one Authority per attack stated. Pool: no longer rolled at hero creation; a faction reward, by the GM's decision. Guild: adopted; earned at Journeyman in The Muster (data/sejr_guilds.json). Polish: escalation d6 table added, so the GM does not have to invent it at the table. v3 audit: Escalation no longer fires on every first plant. v4 audit: object matches the Muster's writ.

name: The Borderlands Tracking Cord
object: A length of braided sinew hung with small carved tokens: a boot print, a feather, a fang, and three others worn unrecognisable by handling. Carried by a tracker from the Doorish Hills who traded it to a Lower Reaches merchant for safe passage through the Cliffs of the Dead. The merchant did not survive the arrangement.
unlock: Track a single creature across at least two sessions without losing the trail, through city, ruin, or wilderness. The creature must be aware it is being hunted, and must have tried to lose you at least once.
risk: Each session you track the creature, the GM rolls a d6. On a 1, it doubles back and ambushes you, and it acts first in the next encounter.

resource.name: Marks
resource.text: Marks (d6 vs. accumulation). Your Mark count is the number of quarries the cord currently tracks. Each quarry takes one token, so the cord tracks no more quarries than it has unburned tokens (six to begin with). Roll 1d6 each time you use a cord ability (Mark a Quarry or Cord Pull), before any new Mark is added. If you roll equal to or below your current Mark count, something near the quarry you are marking or pulling noticed you. A Mark clears when you confront that quarry directly (you end a turn adjacent to it, and it is aware of you), and its token is free for a new quarry; or when you Cut its Mark, and its token burns. Resting does not clear Marks.

powers: Mark a Quarry (1 Action): Touch the cord to any physical trace of a creature: a footprint, a drop of blood, shed skin. Add 1 Mark. While that quarry is marked, you know its general direction and distance within 1 mile regardless of cover or concealment. This works on creatures you have not marked with Hunter's Mark, because the cord marks independently of the class ability.

Cord Pull (Free, 1/encounter): When your marked quarry moves away from you, pull the cord taut. The quarry is Slowed (Speed halved on its next turn). The quarry makes no save, but the cord's d6 still applies. The quarry feels it.

Cut the Mark (Free): Remove one Mark from the cord and burn its token. The cord forgets that quarry, your sense of its direction ends, and it is no longer tracked. Use this when the pursuit is no longer worth the rising risk. Nothing alerts the quarry.
escalation: When the d6 roll triggers, the quarry, or something near it, begins tracking you in return. The GM introduces this threat within 1 to 2 sessions. The threat is proportional to what you marked: a city rat sends a rat, a Borderlands warlord sends soldiers.
design_note: The d6 tracker suits the Hunter's quarry identity. Several Marks make each use riskier, so tracking three creatures at once invites trouble. The cord works beyond sight, which Hunter's Mark does not. Being tracked back is the most Hunter-specific consequence available.
notes: Marks now one count with one clearing rule (confront or Cut); Safe Rest wipe removed; risk line added; em dashes removed; Slowed uses the rules wording. Unlock pass: risk now a per-session d6. Blind audit: Marks had no cap; the cord's own six tokens are now the cap, and Cut the Mark burning a token shrinks it. Pool: no longer rolled at hero creation; a faction reward, by the GM's decision. Guild: adopted; earned at Journeyman in The Wardens' Lodge (data/sejr_guilds.json). v2 audit: Cord Pull says when Slowed applies. v3 audit: confronting frees the token, Cut burns it. Audit round 5: roll before adding the new Mark. Audit round 6: names which quarry notices.

name: The Cracked Lens of Kartan
object: A monocle lens of blue glass, cracked through the centre but held in a copper frame that prevents the crack from spreading. Stamped with the Mages of Kartan's maker's mark on the inner rim. The Mages report it stolen. It has been in a Lower Reaches pawn shop for six months, priced too high for anyone who recognised it, too strange for anyone who didn't.
unlock: Pay the pawn shop's price, which is more than the lens is worth.
Spend a week of downtime studying the crack through the lens, and make an Arcana check, DC 12, to read the maker's mark. On a failure the week is spent and you start over.
Then cast a spell of the highest tier you can cast, with the lens held to your eye for the whole cast.
risk: When the cast ends, the crack pulls at your eye. Make an INT save, DC 13. On a failure the lens fails as its Escalation describes: take 1 Wound, the lens fuses to your face for an hour, and Kartan is told. If you flinch or remove the lens, the crack spreads and it is ruined.

resource.name: Overcharge
resource.text: Overcharge (d6 vs. accumulation). Roll 1d6 each time you cast a tiered spell while wearing the lens, before the spell resolves. The spell takes effect either way. If you roll equal to or below your current Overcharge, the lens fails after the spell (see Escalation). On a safe roll, add 1 Overcharge once (the +1 printed on each power is that same point, not extra), and apply the one safe-roll power that fits you to this spell: Steady Glass before you choose a subclass, then Controlled Upcast or Chaos Bloom. Overcharge clears when you hold the lens to the glass of the Observatory of Infinite Skies through one night.

powers: Controlled Upcast (on a safe roll, +1 Overcharge, Control subclass): The spell gains one Upcast for free.
Chaos Bloom (on a safe roll, +1 Overcharge, Chaos subclass): If you Invoke Chaos with this spell, roll on the Chaos Table with advantage.
Steady Glass (on a safe roll, +1 Overcharge, before you choose a subclass): The spell rolls one extra damage die.

Chaos Sight (Passive, while worn): You see magical auras on creatures and objects within 4 spaces without casting a spell. Illusions appear slightly wrong. Invisible creatures show as a faint shimmer.
escalation: When the d6 triggers, the glass heats to burning. Control Mage: you Lose Control, doing every option on the Control Table, with the GM choosing each time. Chaos Mage: you Invoke Chaos with disadvantage. No subclass yet: you are Dazed until the end of your next turn. Either way you take 1 Wound and cannot remove the lens until the encounter ends, because it has fused to your face. While fused it is inert: no more Overcharge rolls and no safe-roll powers. After the encounter, the Mages of Kartan sense the discharge and know its rough location. They send someone within 1 to 3 sessions. The fusing is now, the visitors are later.
design_note: Differentiated by subclass. The Control Mage gets a free Upcast on safe rolls, a reward for precision, and Lose Control as the failure. The Chaos Mage gets Overcharge relief on safe rolls and a worse Chaos roll on failure. Neither subclass wins both ways. The Mages of Kartan escalation is the City of Arches hook.
notes: Failure now matches the Mage rules (Control mages Lose Control, Chaos mages Invoke Chaos); the 'Control roll' unlock replaced; refill changed from abstention plus rest to a night at the Observatory; costly step and risk added. [TABLE ROLL: whether the Observatory of Infinite Skies lets a visitor leave a lens at its glass overnight.] Unlock pass: added a week of study with an Arcana check, and a d6 on the first cast that can fail the way the item fails. The old unlock was a price and one spell with no real hazard. Blind audit: Chaos mages never gained Overcharge (their safe rolls reduced it), so the lens had no risk for them. Now every safe roll adds 1 Overcharge for both subclasses; the Chaos reward is advantage on Invoke Chaos (a real Mage feature, Master of Chaos). Pool: no longer rolled at hero creation; a faction reward, by the GM's decision. Guild: adopted; earned at Journeyman in The University (data/sejr_guilds.json). Polish: the generic d6 risk became a hazard tied to the object. v3 audit: unlock fuse lasts an hour; no-subclass lines added (subclass comes at level 3). [TABLE ROLL] a Lower Reaches pawn shop is not named in setting/. Audit round 5: the spell resolves first; one safe-roll power per cast.

name: The Broken Verdict
object: A set of golden scales, one pan snapped off and missing. Recovered from the rubble of an old court in the ruins of Sunken Revvia. The remaining pan still tilts when a lie is spoken nearby, or so the merchant who sold it claimed. She may have been lying. The tilt is subtle enough that you cannot always be certain.
unlock: Refuse to deliver a verdict you believe is just, because doing so would protect someone you love.
The refusal must be genuine. The Verdict will know if you were simply afraid.
risk: The GM starts a six-step clock for whoever was owed the verdict. It ticks whenever you are seen shielding the person you chose, and when it fills they act against you both.

resource.name: Held Judgment
resource.text: Held Judgment (toggle, on/off). When your Radiant Judgment would roll Judgment Dice, you may roll them and put them on the scales instead, which turns the toggle on. The scales hold one set of dice at a time, and while they hold it you roll no new Judgment Dice. Held dice stay on the scales past the end of the encounter. The toggle clears when you Release the dice on an attack. If the dice have fused to your Lay on Hands pool (see Escalation), only bringing the scales to the Temple of the Three Sisters clears the fusion.

powers: Hold Judgment (Free, when Judgment Dice would be rolled): Keep the dice on the scales. While they are held, you see the remaining pan tilt when a creature within 6 spaces lies to you, visible only to you. You know. They do not know you know. You must decide what to do with that.
Release (Free, 1/encounter, on a Reach attack): Expend the held dice as Radiant Judgment normally does. This attack's radiant damage ignores armor.
escalation: If the scales hold dice through a full Safe Rest, they fuse with your Lay on Hands pool. You cannot spend from the pool until the scales are cleared at the Temple of the Three Sisters: you perform a Sacred Decree there or, if you know none yet, a priest there absolves you. The temple will want to know why.
design_note: Every time Judgment Dice would roll, the player chooses between spending them on the next attack and holding them for an armor-ignoring release. Holding is paid before the dangerous moment, and the lie-detection stays one-sided, so social scenes become dramatic irony.
notes: Rewritten to fit the Oathsworn rules: Judgment Dice are not spent on reactions (the 'That All You Got?!' line was a Berserker ability) and expire at the end of the encounter, so the card now states that held dice persist. name: The Hollow Contract
object: A slip of black vellum the size of a playing card, written in a language that changes every time you look away. No ink is visible: the text appears to be burned into the material from within. Found pressed between the floorboards of a sealed room in the Lower Reaches, below a building that has been empty for eleven years. The landlord will not say why.
unlock: Patron path: commune with your patron during a Safe Rest and ask it for something you know it does not want to give. Accept its counter-demand before you know what it is.
Reaver path: you have no patron to ask. Read the vellum by your own shadow, in the room where it was found, for three nights, until the language stops changing.
risk: Patron path: the counter-demand is whatever the GM names, and you have already agreed to it. Reaver path: make a WIL save, DC 12, each night, and each failure starts you with 1 Debt before you have any power. Either way, your patron, or the patron you left, learns the contract has a new reader.

resource.name: Debt
resource.text: Debt (pip tracker, max 4). Mark Debt each time you use one of the contract's powers, as each power says. Debt above 4 is lost. Debt clears when the patron collects (see Escalation), or when you carry out a sentence you wrote in the contract: write one sentence in your own blood describing something you will do for the patron, then do it. You must write something real, and you must mean it.

powers: Read the Contract (Free, 1/encounter, mark 1 Debt): Hold the vellum up. You see one true fact about a creature you can see: its most urgent want, its deepest fear, or the name of someone it has wronged.

Patron's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, patron path; every Shadowmancer is on it until choosing a subclass at level 3): You need a use of Pilfered Power (gained at level 2). Spend it to cast a spell from your schools one tier above your current maximum, paying its normal action cost. The patron extends credit.
Reaver's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, Reaver path): Your next Bonescythe strike this turn rolls one extra d12.
escalation: When Debt reaches 4 or more, the patron collects. It does not take power. It adds one sentence about your character to the contract, permanently. The GM decides what it says and reads it aloud. Debt clears. The sentence stays. A Reaver's contract still answers to the patron they left: that patron writes the sentence, and sends an agent to read it to them in person. Roll a d6 on the table below, or choose.
design_note: Debt marks only on the contract's own powers, so it never rides on Pilfered Power, and the Safe Rest commune stays the class's own business. The Reaver path gives patronless Shadowmancers a card of their own. The permanent sentence is the right shape for a relationship with something ancient and dangerous.
notes: Debt no longer marks on Pilfered Power use and the Pilfered Power refill is gone (it duplicated the class commune); Reaver path and Reaver's Margin added (Reavers have no patron and cannot cast tiered spells at this echelon); risk added; em dash removed. Unlock pass: Reaver path now takes three nights with saves; patron path states that the counter-demand binds. Blind audit: the Reaver escalation now says the left patron collects through the stolen contract. Pool: no longer rolled at hero creation; a faction reward, by the GM's decision. Audit round 5: Debt over 4 is lost; collection at 4 or more. Audit round 6: eligibility wording.

name: The Bell of the Three Sisters
object: A small iron handbell, tarnished green at the rim, engraved with three interlinked rings. Identical to the bells carried by the clergy of the Temple of the Three Sisters, except that this one rings slightly differently, a half-note flat or sharp depending on who you ask. The temple says it was never consecrated. They are interested in recovering it for study. They have not offered to pay.
unlock: Heal a creature you expected, and had good reason, to be your enemy, spending healing that an ally needed.
The expectation must be genuine. The bell listens.
risk: The first time you ring it at the Temple of the Three Sisters, the clergy ask who consecrated it. Make an Influence check, DC 14, to answer without lying. On a failure they take the bell for study until you run an errand for them.

resource.name: Resonance
resource.text: Resonance (pip tracker, max 4). Gain 1 Resonance by ringing the bell for an hour over a sickbed or a grave, at the Temple of the Three Sisters or among the tombs of the Cliffs of the Dead, and staying with whoever it is for until the hour ends. Resonance does not clear at a rest. Spent Resonance returns only this way.

powers: Ring Out (Free, spend 1 Resonance): One Dying ally within 6 spaces hears the bell. On its next turn it acts as if it were not Dying: no 1-action limit, and no STR save to attack. It is still Dying, and still takes Wounds from damage.

Chain Heal (Reaction, spend 2 Resonance): When your Lifebinding Spirit heals a creature to maximum HP, the excess healing carries to the nearest damaged ally within 4 spaces. The chain triggers once per Reaction.
Toll (1 Action, spend all 4): Ring the bell loudly. All Dying allies within 6 spaces gain 1 HP and are no longer Dying. You take 1 Wound.
escalation: Spending all 4 Resonance in the Toll cracks the bell's handle. It still rings, but you cannot Toll until a clergyperson of the Three Sisters rehandles it. They will want to know what happened before they agree to help.
design_note: Every power keys off healing, and none of the pool fills from healing, so it adds to the Shepherd's rhythm without rewarding it twice. Chain Heal makes positioning the Spirit a puzzle. The Toll is a first-echelon rescue that costs a Wound and permanently marks the bell. Sacrifice should have weight.

Unlock reworded to 'heal'. Ring no longer gives the Spirit an extra action. Resonance persists through rests. Risk added. Unlock pass: healing must come out of an ally's share; risk now an Influence check that can cost you the bell. name: The Theater of Whispers Setlist
object: A folded sheet of vellum with a handwritten set of songs: titles, keys, and performance notes in the margins in an elegant hand. It belonged to a Songweaver who performed at the Theater of Whispers for fifteen years before disappearing mid-run. The theater kept the setlist. Someone stole it last month. The manager has posted a reward, but is vaguer than expected about what they want to do with whoever took it.
unlock: Perform at the Theater of Whispers, or any venue with an audience of 20 or more, and hold the crowd's full attention for an uninterrupted hour. No skill check. Just perform.
Find someone who heard the setlist's owner perform, and learn the last song, which has no title.
risk: Someone in that crowd knows the hand that wrote the setlist. Make a Perception check, DC 13, to spot them before they leave. On a failure they find you first, within a session.

resource.name: Crowd
resource.text: Crowd (d6 vs. accumulation, max 4). Each time you Call the Song in combat, roll 1d6 against your current Crowd, then add 1 Crowd.
